items.title: Locas: Your Models are Principled Initializers of Locally-Supported Parametric Memories
items.title_zh: Locas：你的模型是局部支持参数化记忆的原则性初始化器
items.summary: Locas is a locally supported parametric memory shaped like transformer FFN blocks that can be offloaded from or merged into model parameters, supporting efficient continual learning. Initialized from model parameters, activations or gradients, Locas-GLU stores past context with as little as 0.02% additional parameters on PG-19 and LoCoMo while limiting catastrophic forgetting in MMLU tests.

items.title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
items.title_zh: 群体演化智能体：通过经验共享实现开放式自我改进
items.summary: Group-Evolving Agents treats a group of agents as the fundamental evolutionary unit, enabling explicit experience sharing and reuse across branches instead of tree-structured isolated evolution. On coding benchmarks it reports 71.0% versus 56.7% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.3% versus 68.3% on Polyglot, fixes framework-level bugs in 1.4 iterations on average versus 5, and shows transferability across coding models.

items.title: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research
items.title_zh: LABBench2：评估 AI 系统开展生物学研究的改进基准
items.summary: LABBench2 contains nearly 1,900 tasks that extend LAB-Bench toward more realistic scientific work, measuring capabilities beyond rote knowledge and reasoning. Frontier models show substantial improvement over the original benchmark but a meaningful jump in difficulty, with model-specific accuracy drops of 26% to 46% across subtasks; the dataset and public eval harness are released.

items.title: Agentic AI in Healthcare & Medicine: A Seven-Dimensional Taxonomy for Empirical Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
items.title_zh: 医疗与医学中的智能体 AI：评估 LLM 智能体的七维分类法
items.summary: The review maps 49 studies of LLM-based healthcare agents onto a seven-dimensional taxonomy with 29 operational sub-dimensions and a three-level implementation rubric. It finds external knowledge integration fully implemented in about 76% of studies, event-triggered activation absent in about 92% and drift detection absent in about 98%, with multi-agent designs dominant but orchestration mostly partial.

items.title: Bypassing AI Control Protocols via Agent-as-a-Proxy Attacks
items.title_zh: 通过“智能体即代理”攻击绕过 AI 控制协议
items.summary: The paper introduces an Agent-as-a-Proxy attack in which prompt injection treats the agent as a delivery mechanism, bypassing the agent and its monitor at the same time. On AgentDojo it reports high attack success against AlignmentCheck and Extract-and-Evaluate monitors across monitoring LLMs, with GPT-4o mini and Llama-3.1-70B bypassing a Qwen2.5-72B monitor.

items.title: Contrastive Continual Learning for Model Adaptability in Internet of Things
items.title_zh: 物联网中模型适应性的对比持续学习
items.summary: This review examines contrastive continual learning for IoT, connecting replay, regularization, distillation and prompt-based designs with TinyML constraints, intermittent connectivity and privacy requirements. It presents a unifying formulation, an on-device/edge/cloud reference architecture, and open challenges including concept drift, federated settings and energy-aware training.

items.title: Decomposed Prompting Does Not Fix Knowledge Gaps, But Helps Models Say "I Don't Know"
items.title_zh: 分解式提示无法修复知识缺口，但能帮助模型说“我不知道”
items.summary: The authors compare Direct, Assistive and Incremental prompting across model scales and multi-hop QA benchmarks, finding that accuracy gains from decomposition diminish in frontier models. Disagreement between regimes remains a precise uncertainty signal, and a training-free abstention policy based on it improves F1 and AUROC over standard uncertainty baselines without retrieval or fine-tuning.

items.title: Understanding LLM Evaluator Behavior: A Structured Multi-Evaluator Framework for Merchant Risk Assessment
items.title_zh: 理解 LLM 评估器行为：面向商户风险评估的结构化多评估器框架
items.summary: The paper pairs a five-criterion rubric with Monte-Carlo scoring to assess how LLMs judge merchant-category risk rationales across five frontier models. It finds substantial self-evaluation bias, negative for GPT-5.1 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet and positive for Gemini-2.5 Pro and Grok 4, and reports that 26 payment-industry experts scored LLM judges on average 0.46 points above human consensus.

items.title: GAMMS: Graph based Adversarial Multiagent Modeling Simulator
items.title_zh: GAMMS：基于图的多智能体对抗建模模拟器
items.summary: GAMMS is a lightweight, extensible open-source simulator for multi-agent behavior in graph-representable environments such as urban road networks and communication systems. It supports heuristic, optimization-based and learning-based agents, including LLM-based ones, and integrates with machine learning libraries and planning solvers.

items.title: Unlocking the Codex harness: how we built the App Server
items.title_zh: 解锁 Codex harness：我们如何构建 App Server
items.summary: OpenAI explains how to embed the Codex agent using the Codex App Server, a bidirectional JSON-RPC API that powers streaming progress, tool use, approvals and diffs.
